items.followUp: What is one difference between a static IP address and a dynamic IP address?

rubric.why: Identifies a defining feature of a static IP address.
rubric.description: Static IP address remains fixed.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a static IP address does not change or is manually assigned.

rubric.why: Identifies how a dynamic IP address is assigned or behaves.
rubric.description: Dynamic IP address is assigned automatically and may change.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it is assigned automatically, usually by DHCP, or may change.

modelAnswer: A static IP address remains fixed and is usually assigned manually.
A dynamic IP address is assigned automatically and may change over time.

items.followUp: Which HTML tag is used to create a hyperlink?

rubric.why: Names the correct HTML tag.
rubric.description: Identifies the table tag.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming `<table>`.

rubric.why: Shows the student knows the purpose of the tag.
rubric.description: States that the tag defines a table.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that it defines or creates a table.

modelAnswer: The `<table>` tag is used to define a table in HTML.

items.followUp: What does the colspan attribute do in an HTML table?

rubric.why: Identifies the attribute being defined.
rubric.description: Names the rowspan attribute.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly identifying `rowspan`.

rubric.why: States the effect of the attribute on a table cell.
rubric.description: Explains that a cell spans multiple rows.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that it makes a cell extend across two or more rows.

modelAnswer: The `rowspan` attribute specifies how many rows a table cell extends across.
It allows one cell to occupy space in multiple rows.

items.followUp: Explain time and space complexity using an example of an algorithm.

rubric.why: Identifies time as a measure of algorithm efficiency.
rubric.description: Mentions time efficiency.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that efficiency can be measured by the time or number of operations an algorithm needs.

rubric.why: Identifies memory use as another efficiency measure.
rubric.description: Mentions space efficiency.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that efficiency can also be measured by memory or storage required.

rubric.why: Provides a relevant algorithm example.
rubric.description: Gives an example of an algorithm.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for using a suitable example, such as searching a list using linear search.

rubric.why: Connects the example to the amount of work performed.
rubric.description: Explains the example's efficiency.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that linear search may check up to n items, so its time grows with the list size.

modelAnswer: Algorithm efficiency can be measured by the time taken or number of operations performed (time efficiency).
It can also be measured by the amount of memory or storage required (space efficiency).
For example, linear search checks the items in a list one by one to find a value.
For a list of n items, it may make up to n comparisons; its time therefore grows with the size of the list.

items.followUp: What is an IP address, and how is an IPv4 address written?

rubric.why: Explains the identifying role of an IP address.
rubric.description: Defines the purpose of an IP address.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing it as a unique address or identifier for a device on a network.

rubric.why: Places IP addressing in its correct context.
rubric.description: Relates the address to network communication.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it identifies a device connected to a network or the Internet.

rubric.why: Gives a key feature of IPv4 format.
rubric.description: Describes IPv4 structure.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that IPv4 uses 32 bits divided into four parts.

rubric.why: Shows understanding of the familiar IPv4 notation.
rubric.description: Gives the notation or a valid example.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the four decimal parts separated by dots, with each part from 0 to 255, or giving a suitable example.

modelAnswer: An IP address is a unique numerical address used to identify a device on a network.
It helps devices identify the source and destination of data sent over the network.
An IPv4 address is 32 bits long and is divided into four parts called octets.
It is written in dotted-decimal form, for example, 192.168.1.1; each part ranges from 0 to 255.

rubric.why: Identifies verification as a checking process.
rubric.description: States that verification involves checking or examining.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing verification as a process of checking, reviewing, or testing.

rubric.why: Explains what verification checks the software against.
rubric.description: Links verification to requirements or specifications.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it checks whether the software or product meets its specified requirements or is being built correctly.

modelAnswer: Verification is the process of checking whether a software product is being developed according to its specified requirements.

items.followUp: What information is commonly placed in the body section of an HTML page?

rubric.why: Identifies the HTML section being described.
rubric.description: Names the head section and its tags.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the section between `<head>` and `</head>`.

rubric.why: Describes the section's contents or display behaviour.
rubric.description: Explains the purpose of the head section.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning information such as the page title or metadata, which generally is not displayed as page content.

modelAnswer: The head section is the part of an HTML page between `<head>` and `</head>`.
It contains information such as the page title and metadata, which is generally not displayed as the page's main content.
